notes: Needs a PiG with Piglet frontend members (D91) and the component kit (D103), which first ship in PiG 0.5.0. Pigpen builds it on PiG 0.5.3, and the member requires SDK v0.5.3. PiG 0.4.1 rejects slots.frontend.

The frontend member draws only when PiG runs directly in a Tern pane (TERM_PROGRAM=tern) with no multiplexer between them (TMUX, STY, ZELLIJ and HERDR_ENV unset). Anywhere else, with PIG_TUI_NATIVE=0 or TERN_TSP=0, or when Tern does not answer the surface protocol hello within a second, PiG draws with its own ANSI renderer.

Native today: user and assistant messages as Markdown, thinking, tool cards (with cancelled status and edit diffs), the working indicator as a Tern spinner, the footer as a Tern status strip, selectors such as /model and /resume as picker sheets, /settings as a prefs sheet, overlays as cards, and the input editor, which takes Tern's edit, undo and send events, so Tern agent blocks and Carly can prompt it. It reports working and idle to Tern with OSC 9;4 terminal progress and names the session file in a hidden pig.session node. Extension components drawn with PiG's component kit (D103), such as pig-music's, become Tern elements, and clicks on them reach the extension as PiG's terminal clicks with the view path, list item and click count. A view's theme overrides are corrected for contrast on Tern's light and dark surfaces. PiG's theme goes to Tern as the program palette and follows Tern's appearance; PiG's mark draws in the settings brand tile; the fullscreen easter eggs play on a Tern screen surface; the footer folder opens in Tern's Files pane; an external editor gets the pane and the surface comes back after. Widgets drawn as raw lines and other extension output still appear as plain lines inside the native surface.

The member uses PiG's component kit and extension mouse delivery (D103), which are in PiG's SDK from 0.5.0 on. A frontend member is fused into a Piglet Binary, so a build needs PiG's source (PIG_SOURCE_ROOT) as for any Piglet with a frontend slot.

It is a Go frontend member on PiG's public SDK and Stencil's Go SDK for Tern (github.com/stencil-hq/tern-sdk/go/tern v0.1.0, MIT): building the Piglet needs a Go toolchain, not Node.js, and network access to the Go module proxy or a warm Go module cache for tern-sdk.

A local Piglet Binary builds and runs in Tern on darwin/arm64, but none is signed or published. The other targets are listed in the manifest and compile-checked only, so no platform is a support claim.
